root_cause.text: The `ieee80211_ml_reconfiguration` function in the mac80211 subsystem fails to validate that the extracted `link_id` is less than `IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS` (15) before using it, allowing a 4-bit `link_id` value of 15 to cause an out-of-bounds write on the `link_removal_timeout[]` array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds a bounds check (`if (link_id >= IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS) continue;`) immediately after extracting `link_id` from the control field. This is supported by the commit message, which states that "link_id is taken from the ML Reconfiguration element (control & 0x000f), so it can be 0..15" while "link_removal_timeout[] has IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS (15) elements, so index 15 is out-of-bounds."

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the `ieee80211_ml_reconfiguration` function. In this function, `link_removal_timeout` is declared as an array of size `IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS` (which is 15). The `link_id` is extracted from the control field using `control & IEEE80211_MLE_STA_RECONF_CONTROL_LINK_ID` (which can be up to 15). The code then writes to `link_removal_timeout[link_id]` without validating that `link_id` is strictly less than `IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS`, leading to an out-of-bounds write when `link_id` is 15.
